summary: Make NFS and SMB3 retention prune safely resumable after partial filesystem deletion. API impact: existing contract (retention and catalog rebuild retry behavior); native interruption acceptance remains open.

guide.reason: Catalog rebuild troubleshooting now explains that a partial NFS/SMB3 prune must settle through the original backup operation before rebuild, and that operators must not erase the intent to force a scan.

api.reason: No route or schema changes. Existing Core retention now records and resumes a validated filesystem delete intent; existing catalog rebuild refuses an in-progress intent and accepts a completed tombstone. Exact backup retry remains the recovery path.

roadmap.reason: Corrects the interrupted-prune safety gate already required by the destination plan.

state.record: Core master catalog and backup run plus a durable hidden delete intent and completion tombstone at the registered repository root. A fresh Controller reads the Core run/catalog; a promoted Core uses the replicated authority and the repository intent to reconcile exact retention work.
state.reason: Controller stores no prune decision or cleanup registry. The destination intent is tied to the Core catalog digest and cannot authorize deleting a protected or pinned point.

verification.method: A focused partial-deletion regression failed before the fix and passed after it; a same-ID replacement regression failed before its manifest check and passed after. Focused race, corrupt-point and retention tests, serial full Go and Python (571 tests, one skip), web tests/typecheck/build, API contract, documentation, diff and repository privacy checks passed. Independent read-only review identified the replacement hazard, then re-reviewed its correction with no further material finding. In a separate disposable NFS/SMB3 fixture, an ignored exact-point pause hook left a matching intent and partial old payload; the fault Core was killed with automatic restart disabled, then a clean current-source capability overlay resumed the retained operation. Exact replay reused the run/point IDs, rebuild succeeded, protected/new points and source hashes survived, and all fixture processes stopped.
verification.limits: The native interruption was controlled fault injection using an ignored hook overlay, not a spontaneous hardware crash. Broader destination faults, a signed release artifact and forge CI remain open.
